paragraphs: Carter Bankshares, Inc. (the "Company") is a bank holding company headquartered in Martinsville, Virginia with assets of $4.9 billion at December 31, 2025. In October 2025, the Company elected to become a financial holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the "BHCA"). As a financial holding company of a Virginia state bank, the Company is subject to regulation, supervision and examination by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the "FRB") and the Bureau of Financial Institutions of the Virginia State Corporation Commission (the "Virginia BFI"). The Company is the parent company of its wholly owned subsidiary, Carter Bank & Trust (the "Bank"). The Bank is a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ("FDIC") insured, Virginia state-chartered bank, which operates 64 branches in Virginia and North Carolina. The Bank became a member of the Federal Reserve System on November 13, 2025. The Bank is subject to regulation, supervision and examination by the FRB (through the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond) and the Virginia BFI. The Company provides a full range of commercial banking, consumer banking, mortgage and services through the Bank. The Company's common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "CARE".
In this Annual Report on Form 10-K, unless the context suggests otherwise, the terms "we," "us" and "our" refer to the Company and its subsidiaries, including the Bank.

The Bank commenced business on December 29, 2006, following the concurrent merger of ten banking institutions. The merged banks and their respective main office locations were: Blue Ridge Bank, N.A. (Floyd, Virginia); Central National Bank (Lynchburg, Virginia); Community National Bank (South Boston, Virginia); First National Bank (Rock Mount, Virginia); First National Exchange Bank (Roanoke, Virginia); Mountain National Bank (Galax, Virginia); Patrick Henry National Bank (Martinsville, Virginia); Patriot Bank, N.A. (Fredericksburg, Virginia); People's National Bank (Danville, Virginia); and Shenandoah National Bank (Staunton, Virginia).

The Company was incorporated on October 7, 2020, to become the Bank's parent bank holding company in a corporate reorganization (the "Reorganization"). Effective November 20, 2020, the Bank merged with a special purpose merger subsidiary of the Company and became a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company. In the Reorganization, each outstanding share of the Bank's common stock was converted into one share of the Company's common stock. Prior to the reorganization, the Company had no material operations. The transaction was completed pursuant to Virginia law and did not require shareholder approval, and the shares issued were exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933.
In October 2025, the Company elected to become a financial holding company under the BHCA. On November 13, 2025, the Bank became a member of the Federal Reserve System.

In the Reorganization, each shareholder of the Bank received securities of the same class, having substantially the same designations, rights, powers, preferences, qualifications, limitations and restrictions, as those that the shareholder held in the Bank.

Prior to the Effective Time, the Bank's common stock was registered under Section 12(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the "Exchange Act"). The Bank was subject to the information requirements of the Exchange Act and, in accordance with Section 12(i) thereof, it filed annual and quarterly reports, proxy statements and other information with the FDIC. Upon consummation of the Reorganization, the Company's common stock was deemed to be registered under Section 12(b) of the Exchange Act, pursuant to Rule 12g-3(a) promulgated thereunder, and the Company now files annual reports, proxy statements and other information with the SEC.

The Company is a financial holding company that conducts its business solely through the Bank. The Bank earns revenue primarily from interest on loans and investment securities and from fees charged for financial services provided to customers. The Bank's principal expenses include interest expense on deposits and borrowings, provision for credit losses, and other
CARTER BANKSHARES, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES ITEM 1. BUSINESS - (continued)
operating expenses, such as salaries and employee benefits, data processing, FDIC insurance assessments, occupancy costs, and income tax provision.

At the close of business on May 23, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of two leased branch facilities and the associated deposits, located in Mooresville, North Carolina and Winston-Salem, North Carolina, from First Reliance Bank (the "Branch Purchase"). In connection with the Branch Purchase, the Bank acquired $55.9 million in deposits, along with cash, personal property, and other fixed assets associated with the branch locations, and welcomed ten associates to its team. No loans were acquired as part of the Branch Purchase.

The Bank offers a full range of deposit products and services to personal and business customers, including noninterest-bearing and interest-bearing checking accounts, savings accounts, retirement accounts money market accounts, and certificates of deposit ("CD") accounts with varying maturities. Deposit products are tailored to the Bank's principal markets and are offered at competitive rates. All deposit accounts are insured by the FDIC up to the maximum amount permitted by law.

The Bank also offers a comprehensive range of commercial and consumer lending products. Commercial lending includes secured and unsecured loans, commercial real estate loans, construction and acquisition loans, and commercial and industrial loans. Consumer lending includes residential mortgage loans, automobile loans, home improvement loans, education loans, overdraft protection, personal loans, credit cards, and other consumer financing products. The Bank originates and holds both fixed-rate and variable-rate mortgage loans and offers home equity lines of credit. The Bank originates residential mortgage loans for which forward sale commitments have been obtained and the loans are expected to be sold shortly after closing.

The Bank's lending activities are subject to various lending limits imposed by federal law. While specific limits may vary depending on the type of loan or borrower relationship, the Bank is generally subject to a loan-to-one-borrower limit equal to 15% of its unimpaired capital and surplus. Loans to directors, officers, associates, or shareholders owning 10% or more of the Company's common stock require approval by the Company's Board of Directors (the "Board") and must be made on terms no more favorable than those available to unaffiliated persons.

headings: Nonperforming assets can take significant time to resolve and may adversely affect the Company's results of operations and financial condition, and could result in additional losses in future periods.
The Company's level of credit risk is elevated due to relationship exposure to the Company's largest credit relationship.
A significant portion of the Company's commercial loan portfolio is secured by real estate, and adverse changes in the real estate market or economic conditions could adversely affect our results.
The Company's concentration in commercial real estate loans, including construction loans, increases its credit risk and could adversely affect its financial condition and results of operations.
A significant part of the Company's lending business is focused on small to medium-sized business which may be impacted more severely during periods of economic weakness.
The Company's allowance for credit losses may be insufficient to absorb expected losses in its loan portfolio, which may adversely affect its business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our real estate lending activities may result in the acquisition of OREO, which could increase expenses and negatively impact our financial condition and results of operations.
Risks Related to Market Conditions, Interest Rates and Investments
The Company's business is subject to interest rate risk and fluctuations in interest rates may adversely affect its earnings, income, cash flow, capital levels and credit quality.
The value of the Company's investment securities could decline.
Inflation could negatively impact the Company's business, its profitability, and its stock price.
Risks Related to the Company's Operations, Cybersecurity and Technology

Failure to keep pace with technological change could adversely affect the Company's business and ability to remain competitive, and it may experience operational challenges when implementing new technologies.
The Company's business is dependent on its executive management team and other key personnel, and the loss of their services could adversely affect its operations.
The Company uses models in its business, and could be adversely affected if its design, implementation, or use of models is flawed.
The Company is subject to physical and financial risks associated with climate change and other weather and natural disaster impacts.
Liquidity risks and adverse developments affecting the financial services industry could materially adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
The Company's liquidity could be adversely affected if it were unable to access short-term funding or monetize liquid assets.
The Company's reliance on customer deposits for funding and liquidity could adversely affect its financial performance if access to such funding becomes impaired.

The Company depends on dividends from its bank subsidiary for substantially all of its revenue, and regulatory restrictions on the Bank's ability to pay dividends could adversely affect its financial condition.
Risks Related to the Company's Business Strategy
The Company's profitability is significantly influenced by economic conditions in the markets that it serves.
The Company faces significant competition from financial institutions and other providers of banking and financial services, which could adversely affect its growth and profitability.
paragraphs: Investments in the Company's common stock involve risks. In addition to the other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the discussion under "Important Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements," investors should carefully consider the risks described below. These risk factors highlight those risks that the Company believes are material; however, they do not necessarily include all risks the Company may face. The inclusion of a risk in the following discussion should not be interpreted to state or imply that the risk has not already materialized.

The risks described below could materially and adversely affect the Company's business, financial condition, liquidity, results of operations, and capital position, and could cause actual results to differ materially from historical results or from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Any such events could adversely affect the trading price of the Company's common stock.

As of December 31, 2025, nonperforming loans ("NPLs") totaled $244.0 million, representing 6.29%, of the Company's loan portfolio. Loans are generally placed on nonaccrual status when the collection of principal or interest is doubtful or when interest or principal payments are 90 days or more past due based on contractual terms.

The Company seeks to reduce or resolve problem assets through a variety of methods, including loan workouts, restructurings, or the sale of loans or underlying collateral. However, declines in collateral values or deterioration in a borrower's financial condition, operating performance, or profitability, as well as actions by borrowers to delay or avoid legal processes, may impede these resolution efforts. As a result, nonperforming assets may persist for extended periods and could continue to adversely affect the Company's business, financial condition and results of operations.

The Company's nonperforming assets (consisting of NPLs and other real estate owned, or "OREO") adversely affect its business, financial condition and result of operations in various ways. The Company does not recognize interest income on nonaccrual loans or OREO, which reduces net income, return on assets, and return on equity. In addition, nonperforming assets increase loan administration and collection costs, negatively impact operating results and the efficiency ratio, and require significant management time and attention, which may detract from other strategic and operational priorities.

If the Company acquires collateral through foreclosure or similar proceedings, the collateral must be recorded as OREO at fair value, which may result in charge-offs or valuation losses. The foreclosure and disposition process also involves legal, carrying, and other costs, which may be significant. An increase in nonperforming assets also increases the Company's risk profile and may affect the minimum capital levels its regulators believe are appropriate in light of such risks. In addition, NPLs and OREO reduce the amount of assets eligible to be pledged as collateral for borrowings from secondary liquidity sources, which may adversely affect liquidity availability.

paragraphs: The following Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A") is intended to assist readers in understanding Carter Bankshares, Inc.'s, operations, financial condition, and current business environment. The MD&A should be read in conjunction with the Company's consolidated financial statements and the accompanying notes included in Item 8. of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.
The MD&A includes the following sections: •Explanation of Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures;
•Critical Accounting Estimates; •The Company's Business and Strategy; •Results of Operations and Financial Condition;
•Capital Resources; •Contractual Obligations; •Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements; •Liquidity;
•Inflation; and •Stock Repurchase Program

This section reviews the Company's financial condition for each of the two most recent years and results of operations for each of the three most recent years. Certain prior-period amounts have been reclassified to conform to the current period presentation. In addition, certain tables may include additional periods to illustrate trends within the Company's consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.
The results of operations presented in the consolidated financial statements are not necessarily indicative of future results.

In addition to results presented in accordance with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles ("GAAP"), management uses, and this Annual Report contains or references, certain non-GAAP financial measures, including interest and dividend income, yield on interest earning assets, net interest income, and net interest margin on a fully taxable equivalent ("FTE") basis.

Management believes these non-GAAP measures are useful because they enhance the ability of investors and management to evaluate and compare the Company's operating results across periods in a meaningful manner. These measures also assist in assessing the Company's underlying operating performance and performance trends and facilitate comparisons with other financial services companies.

The Company believes that presenting interest and dividend income, yield on interest earning assets, net interest income, and net interest margin on an FTE basis improves comparability between income derived from taxable and tax-exempt sources and is consistent with industry practice. Accordingly, GAAP measures presented in the Consolidated Statements of Income are reconciled to their corresponding FTE amounts, including:
•interest and dividend income, •yield on interest earning assets, •net interest income, and
•net interest margin. CARTER BANKSHARES, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS - (continued)
These reconciliations are provided in the "Results of Operations and Financial Condition - Net Interest Income" section of this MD&A for the years ended 2025, 2024 and 2023.

paragraphs: Carter Bankshares, Inc. (the "Company") 為一間以維吉尼亞州馬丁斯維爾為總部的銀行控股公司，截至2025年12月31日，其資產為4.9 十億美元。2025年10月，本公司選擇根據1956年銀行控股公司法案（the "BHCA"），成為財務控股公司。作為一間維吉尼亞州州立銀行的財務控股公司，本公司受美國聯邦儲備系統理事會（the "FRB"）及維吉尼亞州公司委員會財務機構局（the "Virginia BFI"）的監管、監督與檢查。本公司為其全資子公司Carter Bank & Trust（the "Bank"）的母公司。Bank為一間由美國存款保險公司（"FDIC"）投保、維吉尼亞州州立發行的銀行，並在維吉尼亞州及北卡羅萊納州經營64家分行。Bank於2025年11月13日成為美國聯邦儲備系統成員。Bank受FRB（透過裏士滿聯邦儲備銀行）及Virginia BFI的監管、監督與檢查。本公司透過Bank提供完整的商業銀行、消費者銀行、房貸及相關服務。本公司普通股於納斯達克全球選選市場（Nasdaq Global Select Market）交易，股票代碼為"CARE"。
本年度10-K形式年度報告，除非文意另有顯示，否則"we"、"us"及"our"均指本公司及其子公司，包括Bank。

Bank於2006年12月29日開始營運，此為十家銀行機構同時合併後的結果。合併的銀行及其總部為：Blue Ridge Bank, N.A.（Floyd, Virginia）；Central National Bank（Lynchburg, Virginia）；Community National Bank（South Boston, Virginia）；First National Bank（Rock Mount, Virginia）；First National Exchange Bank（Roanoke, Virginia）；Mountain National Bank（Galax, Virginia）；Patrick Henry National Bank（Martinsville, Virginia）；Patriot Bank, N.A.（Fredericksburg, Virginia）；People's National Bank（Danville, Virginia）；以及Shenandoah National Bank（Staunton, Virginia）。

本公司於2020年10月7日成立，以成為Bank的母公司，進行一項公司重組（the "Reorganization"）。2020年11月20日，Bank與本公司之特殊目的合併子公司合併，成為本公司之全資子公司。在重組中，每持有Bank普通股一股，轉換為本公司普通股一股。重組前，本公司無重大營運。此交易依循維吉尼亞州法律進行，不需股東批准，且發行之股票免於根據1933年證券法（the "Securities Act of 1933"）註冊。
2025年10月，本公司選擇根據BHCA成為財務控股公司。2025年11月13日，Bank成為美國聯邦儲備系統成員。
在重組中，每持有Bank普通股之股東，均獲得相同類別之證券，其設計、權利、權限、優先權、資格、限制及限制與其在Bank所持有者 substantially 相同。

在重組生效前，Bank普通股已根據1934年證券交易法（the "Exchange Act"）第12(b)條註冊。Bank受1934年證券交易法資訊要求之約束，並根據該法第12(i)條，提交年度與季度報告、股東授權書及其他資訊予FDIC。重組完成後，本公司普通股根據1934年證券交易法第12(b)條註冊，依該法所頒之Rule 12g-3(a)規定，本公司現於SEC提交年度報告、股東授權書及其他資訊。
本公司為一間財務控股公司，其業務 solely 透過Bank進行。Bank主要透過貸款及投資證券之利息收入，以及為客戶提供財務服務所收取之費用來獲取營業收入。Bank之主要費用包括存款及借款之利息支出、信貸損失準備及其他
CARTER BANKSHARES, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES ITEM 1. BUSINESS - (continued)
營運費用，例如薪資及員工福利、資料處理、FDIC保險費、營業場地費用及所得稅提列。
於2025年5月23日營業日閉市時，本公司完成取得位於北卡羅來納州摩爾斯維爾及溫斯頓-塞勒姆的兩處租賃分行據點及其相關存款，來自First Reliance Bank（"分行購置"）。配合分行購置，銀行取得55.9 百萬美元存款，並取得與分行據點相關的現金、個人財產及其他固定資產，並迎來十位同仁加入團隊。分行購置並未取得貸款。
銀行提供完整之存款產品與服務予個人及企業客戶，包括免息及有息支票帳戶、儲蓄帳戶、退休帳戶、貨幣市場帳戶，以及不同到期日之定期存款帳戶（"定期存款"）。存款產品根據銀行主要市場進行設計，並提供具有競爭力之利率。所有存款帳戶均受FDIC保險，保險金額以法律所允許之最高額為限。

銀行亦提供廣泛之商業及消費者貸款產品。商業貸款包括擔保及無擔保貸款、商業不動產貸款、建設及購置貸款，以及商業及工業貸款。消費者貸款包括住宅抵押貸款、汽車貸款、住宅裝修貸款、教育貸款、 overdraft 保護、個人貸款、信用卡及其他消費者融資產品。銀行發放並持有固定利率及變動利率之住宅抵押貸款，並提供住宅貸款之房屋貸款線信用額度。銀行發放住宅抵押貸款，已取得未來銷售承諾，並預期在貸款關閉後不久即出售。
銀行之貸款業務受美國聯邦法律所設之貸款額度限制。雖然特定貸款類型或借款人關係之限制可能有所不同，但銀行一般而言受貸款對單一借款人之限制，為其未受損害資本及盈餘之15%。對董事、高階主管、同仁或持有本公司普通股10%或以上之股東之貸款，需經本公司董事會（"董事會"）批准，且貸款條件不得優於對非關係人所提供的條件。

paragraphs: 以下為管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析（"MD&A"），旨在協助讀者瞭解Carter Bankshares, Inc.之營運、財務狀況與目前之商業環境。MD&A應與本公司合併財務報表及附註說明（包含於本年度10-K表格第8項）一併閱讀。
MD&A包含以下各節：•非GAAP財務指標之使用說明；
•關鍵會計估計；•本公司之業務與策略；•營運成果與財務狀況；
•資本資源；•契約義務；•表外安排；•流動性；
•通貨膨脹；以及•股票回購計畫
本節回顧本公司最近兩年之財務狀況及最近三年之營運成果。某些前一時期之金額已重新分類，以符合當前時期之呈現方式。此外，某些表格可能包含更多時期，以說明本公司合併財務報表及相關揭露之趨勢。
合併財務報表中呈現之營運成果並不一定代表未來之結果。
除依美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）所呈現之結果外，管理層亦使用非GAAP財務指標，且本年度報告包含或參考這些指標，包括利息及股息收入、利息產生資產之收益率、淨利息收入，以及以完全課稅等價（"FTE"）為基礎之淨利息邊際率。
本公司認為這些非GAAP指標是有用的，因為它們能提升投資人與本公司管理階層評估與比較本公司營運成果的能力，並以有意義的方式進行跨期間比較。這些指標也協助評估本公司本質上的營運績效與績效趨勢，並促進與其他金融服務機構的比較。
本公司認為，以FTE基礎呈現利息與股息收入、利息產生資產的收益率、淨利息收入與淨利息邊際，可提高來自課稅與非課稅來源收入之間的可比性，並符合產業慣例。因此，於合併損益表中呈現的GAAP指標已彙整至對應的FTE金額，包括：
•利息與股息收入、•利息產生資產的收益率、•淨利息收入，以及
•淨利息邊際。CARTER BANKSHARES, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
項目7. 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析 - （續）
這些彙整資訊已於本MD&A的『營運成果與財務狀況 - 淨利息收入』部分，針對2025年、2024年及2023年財務年度提供。

headings: 不良資產可能需要相當長的時間才能解決，並可能對本公司的營運成果與財務狀況產生不利影響，並可能導致未來期間產生額外的虧損。
由於與本公司最大信用關係的關係風險，本公司的信用風險程度較高。
本公司商業貸款組合的很大一部分是以不動產為擔保，不動產市場或經濟條件的不利變化可能對我們的營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司在商業不動產貸款，包括建設貸款方面的集中度，會增加其信用風險，並可能對其財務狀況與營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司貸款業務的很大一部分專注於中小型企業，這些企業在經濟疲軟時期可能受到更嚴重的影響。
本公司的信用損失準備金可能不足以吸收貸款組閤中預期的虧損，這可能對其業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生不利影響。
我們的不動產貸款業務可能導致取得不良資產（OREO），這可能會增加費用，並對我們的財務狀況與營運成果產生負面影響。
與市場條件、利率及投資相關的風險
本公司的業務面臨利率風險，利率波動可能對其獲利、收入、現金流、資本水準及信用品質產生負面影響。
本公司投資證券的價值可能下跌。
通貨膨脹可能對本公司業務、其獲利能力及股票價格產生負面影響。
與本公司營運、網路安全及科技相關的風險
若無法跟上科技變革的節奏，可能對本公司業務及維持競爭力的能力產生負面影響，並可能在實施新科技時遭遇營運挑戰。
本公司業務依賴其高階管理團隊及其他關鍵人員，若失去其服務，可能對其營運產生負面影響。
本公司在業務中使用模型，若其模型的設計、實施或使用有瑕疵，可能對其產生負面影響。
本公司面臨與氣候變遷及其他天氣及自然災害影響相關的實體及財務風險。
流動性風險及對金融服務業產生的不利發展可能重大且負面地影響本公司的財務狀況及營運結果。
若本公司無法取得短期資金或套現流動資產，其流動性可能受到不利影響。
本公司依賴客戶存款作為資金及流動性來源，若無法取得此類資金，可能對其財務表現產生不利影響。
本公司 substantially all 的收入來自於銀行子公司之股息，而對銀行子公司支付股息的監管限制可能對其財務狀況產生不利影響。
與本公司業務策略相關的風險
本公司獲利能力大幅受其所服務市場之經濟條件影響。

paragraphs: 投資於本公司普通股涉及風險。除本年度10-K表報表中包含的其他資訊，包括「重要向前看聲明」的討論外，投資人應謹慎考量下列風險。這些風險因素突顯本公司認為重要的風險；然而，它們並不必然包含本公司可能面臨的所有風險。下列討論中提及的風險，不應被解釋為表示或暗示該風險尚未實現。
下列所描述的風險可能對本公司的業務、財務狀況、流動性、營運結果及資本地位造成重大且不利的影響，並可能導致實際結果與歷史結果或本年度10-K表報表中所包含的向前看聲明預期結果有重大差異。任何此類事件可能對本公司普通股的交易價格造成不利影響。
截至2025年12月31日，不良貸款（"NPLs"）總計為244.0 百萬美元，佔本公司貸款組合的6.29%。貸款通常在本金或利息回收存在疑慮，或利息或本金付款逾期90天或以上（根據契約條款）時，被歸類為不良貸款。
本公司透過多種方式努力減少或解決問題資產，包括貸款協議、貸款重整，或出售貸款或其背後的擔保品。然而，擔保品價值下降或借款人財務狀況、營運表現或獲利能力惡化，以及借款人延遲或避免法律程序的行動，可能阻礙這些解決措施。因此，不良資產可能持續一段長時間，並可能繼續對本公司的業務、財務狀況及營運結果造成不利影響。
本公司的不良資產（包含不良貸款及其它實質財產，或"OREO"）以多種方式對其業務、財務狀況及營運結果造成不利影響。本公司不對不良貸款或OREO認列利息收入，這會降低淨收入、資產回報率及權益回報率。此外，不良資產會增加貸款管理及回收成本，對營運結果及效率比率產生負面影響，並需要大量管理時間與關注，這可能影響其他戰略及營運優先事項。
若本公司透過拍賣或類似程序取得擔保品，該擔保品必須按公允價值記錄為OREO，這可能會導致核銷或評價損失。拍賣及處置程序也涉及法律、持有及其他成本，這些成本可能相當顯著。不良資產增加也會提高本公司的風險敞口，並可能影響其監管機構認為在考慮到這些風險後適當的最低資本水平。此外，NPLs及OREO會減少可用作從第二來源流動性融資擔保品的資產數量，這可能會對流動性可得性造成不利影響。
